text:
sara_support: @mike_runtime heads up — Cassiopeia (customer) hit ~15% 429s for their dedicated pool last night and are seeing auth-related spikes in p99 latency. They say it started after a token rotation and an ad-hoc campaign.

mike_runtime: can you paste the error pattern? 429s vs timeouts? any 5xx?

cassiopeia_ops: we saw mostly 429s and a few 502s. p50 barely moved but p95/p99 jumped. auth latencies spiked to 1.2s for token fetch, causing many in-flight requests to pile up. billing showed unexpected higher token consumption around 03:10 UTC.

sara_support: repro steps from customer:
1) steady baseline qps ~180
2) sudden campaign bump to 600 qps for ~4m
3) token rotation + short-lived bursty clients
4) ~03:10 429 wave and higher per-request latency

luis_support: logs they attached include many lines like:
```
2026-10-12T03:10:12Z WARN request=abc123 pool=ded-cassiopeia reason=rate_limited status=429 throttle_reason=pool_capacity_exceeded
2026-10-12T03:10:13Z INFO auth token_fetch_ms=1200 user=cassiopeia/ingest
```

ali_oncall: quick hypothesis: pool headroom exhausted + autoscale cooldown too long to react to 3-4m spike. token rotation added synchronous latency so per-request duration increased -> effective capacity drop -> cascading 429s.

mike_runtime: agree. I also see noisy-tenant signatures: uneven heat map, some client IPs were sending very short requests with high concurrency. If KV cache prefixing didn't hit, we lose batching efficiency.

tim_sre: can we confirm Dedicated pool config: guaranteed_slots, max_instances, autoscale_policy? Also warmup settings?

sara_support: Cassiopeia provided their pool config in the support ticket:
- guaranteed_slots: 8
- max_instances: 20
- autoscale: cpu-based, scale_up_threshold=75%, cooldown=180s, burst_buffer=0.
- model: llama-13B-q4 and q8 fallback

mike_runtime: burst_buffer=0 is the smoking gun. With short spikes you need headroom or faster scale. Also cpu-based scaling lags for token-latency-induced throughput loss. Recommend weight-by-latency or request-rate policy + set burst_buffer >= 30%.

jess_account: customer asked about immediate mitigations and any billing anomalies — they saw a ~2x billing delta on token units around the spike window. Is that expected with retries and longer request durations?

mike_runtime: retries and increased tokenization per request shouldn't double token billing. Likely they retried clients plus extra tokens from repeated context sends. Need to correlate request ids and retry loops.

cassiopeia_ops: we did see our client SDK retry aggressively on 429, default backoff was 200ms x 4. We can change client-side backoff but want Redwood to avoid 429s first.

luis_support: short-term actions:
- bump pool burst_buffer to 40% (adds immediate headroom)
- reduce autoscale cooldown to 60s and enable request-rate signal
- temporarily increase max_instances from 20 -> 30
- enable token-cache warmup for expected model

mike_runtime: I can apply the burst_buffer + autoscale change for them. Will monitor. Also suggest pinning to q8 variant for lower latency during campaign.

deploy-bot: deployment started by mike_runtime at 2026-10-12T03:25:12Z: patch autoscale policy and burst_buffer for pool ded-cassiopeia.

ops-bot: alert suppressed for ded-cassiopeia 03:25:17Z while rolling change.

ali_oncall: after change we should run a short synthetic replay of the 600 qps spike to validate behavior. mike, can you queue a repro run?

mike_runtime: queued a controlled replay from canary harness for 5m at 620 qps starting 03:32 UTC. Will post results.

cassiopeia_ops: thanks — we'll pause our campaign until you confirm. Also we fixed client backoff config just in case.

mike_runtime: results: 03:32 run finished — p99 latency dropped from 1.2s -> 320ms, 429s went from 15% -> 0.7%. CPU utilization stayed under 70% and autoscaler added 6 instances within 60s. No billing spike observed in replay window.

jess_account: sharing outcome with customer and offering a billing review window for the spike hour. Recommend follow-up: run canary during next campaign and also set an SLA policy for reserved headroom if they expect repeated bursts.

tim_sre: long-term follow-ups:
- recommend changing autoscale policy default for high-burst customers to include request-rate signal and lower cooldowns.
- provide a playbook for token rotations during campaign windows (stagger rotations, pre-warm token caches).

luis_support: I'll update support KB with a short checklist: burst_buffer, autoscale signals, client backoff, pin model quantization, and warmup for rotations.

sara_support: closing notes: customer paused campaign, changes applied, replay verified. Next steps: (1) billing check by jess_account, (2) SRE review of autoscale defaults, (3) KB update by luis_support. Marking thread resolved unless customer reopens. :white_check_mark:
